nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. For $y, x \in F^d$, the affine line with base point $y$ and direction $x$ is the set $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq F^d$. When $x = 0$ this set is the single point $\{y\}$.
nodes.title: Affine line

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. For $x, y \in F^d$, the dot product is $x \cdot y = \sum_{i} x_i y_i \in F$, the sum running over the $d$ coordinates.
nodes.title: Dot product

nodes.summary: There is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every finite field $F$ and every Kakeya set $E \subseteq F^3$, that is, a set such that for every $x \in F^3$ there is $y \in F^3$ with $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq E$, we have $|E| \ge c\,|F|^3$.
nodes.title: Finite field Kakeya sets in dimension three have cubic size

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every finite field $F$ and every Kakeya set $E \subseteq F^3$, that is, a set such that for every $x \in F^3$ there is $y \in F^3$ with $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq E$, we have $|E| \ge c\,|F|^3$.
nodes.title: Statement of the finite field Kakeya bound in dimension three

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $d$ a natural number and $\chi$ an additive character of $F$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. For $\mu : F^d \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\xi \in F^d$, the Fourier transform of $\mu$ at $\xi$ is $\hat{\mu}(\xi) = \sum_{x \in F^d} \chi(-\xi \cdot x)\, \mu(x) \in \mathbb{C}$, where $\xi \cdot x$ is the dot product.
nodes.title: Finite-field Fourier transform

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $K \subseteq F^d$ be a Kakeya set and let $\chi$ be a nontrivial additive character of $F$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. Then, first, there is a probability measure $\mu$ on $K$ whose Fourier transform $\hat{\mu}$ with respect to $\chi$ satisfies $|\hat{\mu}(\xi)| \le q^{-1}$ for every nonzero $\xi \in F^d$. nodes.title: Fraser's Fourier decay theorem for finite-field Kakeya sets

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. A set $K \subseteq F^d$ is a Kakeya set if for every $x \in F^d$ there is $y \in F^d$ such that the affine line $\{y + a x : a \in F\}$ is contained in $K$; that is, $K$ contains a line in every direction.
nodes.title: Kakeya set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $d$ a natural number and $K \subseteq F^d$. A function $\mu : F^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a probability measure on $K$ if $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in F^d$, $\sum_{x \in F^d} \mu(x) = 1$, and $\mu(x) \ne 0$ implies $x \in K$.
nodes.title: Probability measure supported on a set

nodes.summary: For a type $F$ and a natural number $d$, $F^d$ denotes the set of $d$-tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of elements of $F$, that is, functions from a $d$-element index set to $F$.
nodes.title: Coordinate space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
